battle.title: Shortest Path Showdown
battle.description: Race through weighted graphs and find where Dijkstra shines or breaks.

questions.text: What does Dijkstra's algorithm compute, and under what condition is it correct?
options: Shortest distances between all pairs, for any edge weights
Shortest distances from one source, provided all edge weights are non-negative
The minimum spanning tree, for any edge weights
Shortest distances from one source, even with negative edges
questions.answer: Shortest distances from one source, provided all edge weights are non-negative
questions.explanation: Dijkstra is a single-source algorithm that relies on weights never decreasing a path. Negative edges break its greedy finalisation.

questions.text: This Dijkstra over a matrix starts at vertex 0 (1000 means no edge). What does it print?
questions.explanation: Vertex 2 is reached at 1, which then improves vertex 1 from 4 to 3 and vertex 3 from 9 to 8 via 1. Using only direct edges from 0 gives the wrong [0, 4, 1, 9].

questions.text: A road map has positive travel times on each road. You need the fastest time from your home to every other town. Which approach fits?
options: Plain BFS counting the number of roads
DFS exploring every path and keeping the smallest
Sorting the roads by time and taking the cheapest first
questions.explanation: Dijkstra respects different edge weights. BFS minimises the number of edges, not total time, and trying all DFS paths is exponential.

questions.text: What is the running time of Dijkstra with a binary-heap priority queue on a graph with V vertices and E edges?
questions.explanation: Each edge may cause a heap insert costing O(log V), plus vertex pops. O(V + E) is BFS, which cannot handle weights.

questions.text: Edges: A->B weight 4, A->C weight 5, C->B weight -3. Dijkstra from A finalises B when popping it. What does it report for B?
options: 2, because it will notice the negative edge
4, and that is the true shortest distance
4, but the true shortest distance is 2 via C
questions.answer: 4, but the true shortest distance is 2 via C
questions.explanation: B is popped with distance 4 before C is processed, and it is never revisited, so the cheaper route A-C-B (5 - 3 = 2) is missed. This is exactly why negative edges are not allowed.

coding.title: Cheapest Route Home
coding.description: A network has n towns numbered 1 to n and m two-way roads, each with a positive or zero travel cost. Find the minimum total cost to travel from town 1 to town n. If town n cannot be reached print -1. Use Dijkstra with a priority queue; the answer can exceed 32-bit range in principle, so use long.
coding.inputDescription: Line 1: n and m. Then m lines each with u v w (a road between u and v with cost w).
coding.outputDescription: A single integer: the minimum cost, or -1 if unreachable.
